question.knowledge_point: Calculating a Joint Probability From a Table
question.problem:
|  | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | $Y=6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |

Compute $P((X,Y)\in {(1,4),(1,6),(2,6)})$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.

judgment.reasoning: All 16 mathematical answers agree with their own captured worked solutions. q-73625 has pivots in columns 2, 3, and 4, hence rank 3. q-35734 reduces to pivots in columns 1, 2, and 3; its solution mistakenly names the matrix B instead of P, but the reduction and answer are correct. q-131302 has pivots in columns 1, 2, and 4 after exchanging the last two rows. For q-130256, yy' makes I nonlinear, while II and III are linear combinations of derivatives with coefficients depending only on x. Linearity gives 10 for q-64900 and x²−1 for q-79606. For q-181958, option 2 contains exactly (p,w), (q,w), (p,z), and (q,z), matching the completed source diagram despite different cropping. Cartesian-product cardinalities are 10·10=100 and 7·6=42. The homogeneous equations give Ae^(−6x) and Ae^(5x). Substituting y_p=x²/2−x gives 2y_p'+2y_p=x²−2. The probability answers follow respectively from the indicated cell, summing three disjoint cells, summing four cells in the union without double counting, and summing the X=2 row. No submitted grades or earlier answers were supplied; confirmation rests on the captured worked solutions.
